Question: Note that statistical tables are not necessary to answer this question. For a sample of 1000 observations, the Dickey-Fuller test statistic values are

Options: 
A. Equal to those in the left hand tail of a normal distribution
B. Less negative than (i.e. smaller in absolute value than) those in the left hand tail of a normal distribution
C. Obtained from a standard normal distribution
D. Obtained from an analytical formula for the density of the Dickey-Fuller distribution
E. More negative than (i.e. bigger in absolute value than) those in the left hand tail of a normal distribution
F. More negative (i.e. bigger in absolute value) for a 10% size of test than a 5% test.
G. Less negative than (i.e. smaller in absolute value than) those in the right hand tail of a normal distribution

Provide the correct letter choice in \boxed{X}, where X is the correct letter choice. Keep the explanation or feedback within 3 sentences.

*   The Dickey-Fuller test is used to test for a unit root in a time series.
*   Under the null hypothesis of a unit root, the test statistic does *not* follow a standard normal distribution (or a $t$-distribution).
*   It follows a non-standard distribution (often called the Dickey-Fuller distribution).
*   This distribution is skewed to the left (negative skew).
*   Consequently, the critical values for the DF test are *more negative* (i.e., larger in absolute value) than the critical values from the standard normal distribution (or the $t$-distribution) for the same significance level.
    *   Example: For a 5% level, the standard normal critical value is approx -1.645. The DF critical value (depending on sample size and model specification) is usually around -2.86 or -2.90 for large samples.

Obtained from an analytical formula for the density of the Dickey-Fuller distribution:** While there are integral representations, critical values are typically obtained from simulation tables (MacKinnon).
